title: A drum kit's named pads land on the usual drum notes
description:
As a beatmaker, I want a drum kit's named pads on the notes drummers expect (kick on C1, snare on D1, closed hat on F#1), so that the rack plays with any drum pattern and controller mapping.

The full word-to-note table lives in `design/daw-presets.md` (from M0); these scenarios pin the common words and the rule for the rest.

```gherkin
Feature: A drum kit exported with its pads on the usual drum notes
  Background:
    Given one-shot samples "k.wav", "s.wav", "h.wav", "o.wav", "c.wav", "z.wav" and "y.wav", analyzed
    And the score "kit.apr":
      """
      tempo 96
      key C
      clip k = k.wav
      clip s = s.wav
      clip h = h.wav
      clip o = o.wav
      clip c = c.wav
      clip z = z.wav
      clip y = y.wav
      kit drums
        kick  = k
        snare = s
        hat   = h
        open  = o
        crash = c
        zap   = z
        yell  = y
      """

  Scenario Outline: Drum words land on their usual notes
    When I export kit "drums" from "kit.apr"
    Then pad "<pad>" is on note <note>

    Examples:
      | pad   | note |
      | kick  | C1   |
      | snare | D1   |
      | hat   | F#1  |
      | open  | A#1  |
      | crash | C#2  |

  Scenario: Other names fill the free notes from C1 upward, in alphabetical order
    When I export kit "drums" from "kit.apr"
    Then pad "yell" is on note C#1
    And pad "zap" is on note D#1

  Scenario: A pad that holds another kit's slice plays that slice
    Given the score "kit.apr" also says "kit b = slice k by beats 0.5" and the pad "rim = b.2"
    When I export kit "drums" from "kit.apr"
    Then pad "rim" plays "k.wav" from the second slice's start to its end

  Scenario: Pads are named in the rack
    When I export kit "drums" from "kit.apr"
    Then each pad's chain is named after its pad ("kick", "snare", ...)
```
